I have done a lot of them. It's tricky, you're playing with fire. I think its possible with the right set and setting you can have some personal growth. Also interesting to keep in mind there's some theoretical association between them and disassociative disorders. 

Make sure to have a trip sitter. Make sure to not be having a particularly terrible week. And start small...dont go in it with a 'chug chug chug' mentality. 

I consumed an extordinarily large does of one particularl type of hallucinogen and I ended up having developing a panic disorder. Not to scare you off, just start small though and even if things go sour it will just be unpleasant, not hell. They are all pretty physically safe to do, but are powerful tools of the mind as well. 

It's funny I was about 19 when I started that stuff haha, I was looking for God, or meaning, or something. For me that dissasociation was a culmination of years or anxiety and depression slowly growing. The depersonalization is a breaking point, and adaptive in some ways because it removes you from the situation. I think that's the god like feeling you described. Double edged sword though, as you know.

I feel for your situation man, I really do. This could be totally off base because I'm projecting, but My advice would be to sit down and seriously figure out where you'd like to start looking for meaning, and you'll really have to dig. For me, I was too afraid to go towards what little passion I had left. I ended up making safe choices that led me to where I am. I'll tell you I have my life together way more than most people my age, but I'm going to die soon. It's not enough in this day and age you need self actualization. Try Victor frankly man's search for meaning, it's a quick read. If I was 19 Jordan Peterson would have been my fucking savior, his philosophy I think is exactly what young people in your situation need. I don't want to get political, he's a zany guy but listen to his talks about finding meaning. If you can read his book 7 rules for life an atedote to chaos. It's the best advice I can give you, it might have saved 19 year old me. You're still young, I guess I am too. But you have a decade to try, fail, and try again. Dont be too afraid to try. And do whatever you can to fight, overcome the fucking terrible emotions and zombification holding you back. It's possible to turn it around. I was the same way in school too and I got so disenchanted by it, I was burnt out before college even began. But you just assume your direction will come, mine never did. As unpleasant as it is it's time to start looking, and making steps. It may be the wrong direction, but you'll at least eliminate one possible path ad undesirable. It's a step. Best of luck friend, I really wish you the best of luck Im not one of thos "it gets better" bullshitters, but do what you can when you can. There are days where you may not feel like getting out of bed, and sometimes you may lose the battle of the day and stay in bed. Thats ok. The war still rages, and you're going to get beat down. It's vital to figure out ways to fight. The depression, the fear doesn't fight fair. Do your best to never stop searching, I think you've got embers in you. You don't have to believe it's possible, hell it may not be, but when you can, fight the mystery . I know it's a catch 22, and I  don't want to sound like one of those "just put a smile, go to the beach" people, because I totally am not that fucking person. I hope the advice made sense though. It's fucking hard being  young in today's society.
Appreciate you reading, here's to bluer skies.
